questions.question: Why are ultrasounds preferred for cleaning objects with complex shapes?

options.text: They have very high speed in liquids
Their high frequency dislodges dirt particles

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Their high frequency dislodges dirt particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ultrasound cleaning** uses high-frequency sound waves, typically above 20 kHz, to create rapid pressure changes in a liquid medium. These sound waves generate microscopic bubbles in the liquid through a process called **cavitation**.
 
• When these bubbles collapse, they release a tremendous amount of energy in the form of shock waves. This energy **dislodges dirt, debris, and contaminants** from surfaces, especially in hard-to-reach areas.
 
• The high frequency of ultrasound waves ensures thorough cleaning of objects with **complex shapes, intricate designs, or delicate surfaces**, such as jewelry, lenses, surgical instruments, or electronic components.
 
• Unlike traditional cleaning methods, ultrasound cleaning is **non-abrasive**, making it ideal for fragile or sensitive materials where physical scrubbing could cause damage.
 
• This technology is widely used in various industries, including **medical, automotive, electronics, and manufacturing**, due to its efficiency and precision in cleaning intricate objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cavitation:**

 
 
• Cavitation refers to the formation and collapse of microscopic bubbles in a liquid due to high-frequency sound waves.
 
• This process is the key mechanism behind ultrasound cleaning, as the collapsing bubbles release energy that effectively removes dirt and contaminants.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ultrasound Cleaning:**
 
 
• **Medical Industry:** Used for cleaning surgical instruments, dental equipment, and laboratory tools.
 
• **Jewelry:** Cleans intricate jewelry pieces without causing damage to delicate stones or metalwork.
 
• **Electronics:** Removes dust and contaminants from circuit boards and electronic components.
 
• **Automotive:** Cleans fuel injectors, carburetors, and other small engine parts.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Ultrasound Cleaning:**
 
 
• It is highly effective in cleaning objects with **complex geometries**, such as threads, holes, and grooves.
 
• It eliminates the need for harsh chemicals or abrasive scrubbing, making it an **eco-friendly** and safe cleaning method.
 
• The process is fast, efficient, and can clean multiple objects simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Ultrasound Cleaning:**
 
 
• It may not be suitable for cleaning **soft materials** or items prone to damage from cavitation forces.
 
• Specialized equipment and expertise are required to operate ultrasonic cleaners effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **High Speed in Liquids:** Ultrasound waves do not rely on speed in liquids for cleaning but on their ability to create cavitation bubbles. Hence, this is not the correct explanation.
 
• **Temperature Increase:** While ultrasound cleaning can slightly increase the liquid's temperature, this is not the primary mechanism for dislodging dirt particles.
 
• **Magnetic Effect:** Ultrasound cleaning does not involve magnetic effects. It relies on acoustic energy and cavitation.

questions.question: The ability of gases to be compressed easily is due to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**large spaces between particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Compressibility of gases**: Gases are highly compressible due to the **large spaces between particles**. This allows gas particles to be pushed closer together when pressure is applied.
 
• **Interparticle forces**: In gases, the intermolecular forces are **negligible**, which means the particles can move freely and occupy more space in comparison to liquids or solids.
 
• **Particle arrangement**: Gas particles are **randomly arranged** and are far apart from one another, which accounts for their high compressibility.
 
• **Kinetic energy of particles**: Gas particles have a high amount of **kinetic energy**, which keeps them in constant motion and prevents them from forming a fixed structure.
 
• **Effect of pressure**: When external pressure is applied to a gas, the large spaces between the particles get reduced, making it easier to compress gases into smaller volumes. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Properties of gases:**

 
 
• Gases have **no fixed shape** or volume and take the shape of their container.
 
• The particles in gases move freely and randomly, contributing to their ability to fill any container completely.
 
• Gases exhibit **low density** compared to liquids and solids due to the large spaces between their particles.
 
• They can be easily compressed because of the **availability of empty spaces** between particles.
 
 
 
• **Effect of pressure and temperature:**
 
 
• When pressure is applied to gases, the particles come closer, reducing the volume (Boyle’s Law).
 
• Increasing temperature increases the kinetic energy of gas particles, causing them to move faster and occupy more space (Charles’s Law).
 
 
 
• **Comparison with liquids and solids:**
 
 
• Solids have closely packed particles with strong intermolecular forces, making them incompressible.
 
• Liquids have particles that are close but can slide past each other, leading to low compressibility compared to gases.
 
• Gases, with their large particle spacing and negligible forces, are **highly compressible**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of gas compressibility:**
 
 
• Compressed natural gas (**CNG**) is stored under high pressure due to the compressibility of gases.
 
• Oxygen cylinders used in medical facilities are filled by compressing oxygen gas.
 
• In refrigeration systems, gases are compressed to transfer heat effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Boyle’s Law:** States that at a constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume. This explains how compressibility is possible in gases when external pressure is applied.
 
• **Charles’s Law:** Explains the relationship between temperature and volume in gases. With an increase in temperature, gases expand due to increased particle movement.
 
• **Applications of gas compressibility:** Found in industries like **petroleum refining, medical oxygen supply**, and transportation of compressed gases such as **hydrogen and methane**.
 
• **Real-life example:** Car tires are inflated with compressed air, utilizing the high compressibility of gases to support the vehicle's weight.

questions.question: When light enters a glass prism from air at the first refracting surface, the light ray _________.

options.text: Bends towards the normal, as it enters a denser medium
Bends away from the normal, increasing the angle of incidence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bends towards the normal, as it enters a denser medium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When light travels from a less dense medium (air) to a denser medium (glass), its speed decreases. This change in speed causes the light ray to **refract towards the normal** at the boundary between the two media.
 
• The bending of light at the interface is governed by **Snell's Law**, which states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
 
• The refractive index of glass is higher than that of air, meaning glass is optically denser. As a result, the light ray bends **towards the normal** when entering glass.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because the wavelength of light decreases in the denser medium, while its frequency remains unchanged.
 
• The bending of light as it enters the glass prism is the fundamental principle behind various optical phenomena, including dispersion and the formation of rainbows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Snell’s Law:**

 
 
• Snell's Law is expressed as: **n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂**, where **n₁** and **n₂** are the refractive indices of the first and second media, and **θ₁** and **θ₂** are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively.
 
• The refractive index is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced in a given medium compared to its speed in a vacuum.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Refraction:**
 
 
• Refraction is used in the design of optical instruments such as lenses, microscopes, telescopes, and cameras.
 
• It is also responsible for phenomena like mirages and the apparent bending of objects submerged in water.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion in a Prism:**
 
 
• When white light enters a prism, it is refracted at different angles for different wavelengths, causing the light to spread out into its constituent colors.
 
• This separation of light into colors is called **dispersion** and is the principle behind the formation of rainbows.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection:**
 
 
• Total internal reflection occurs when light attempts to move from a denser medium to a less dense medium at an angle greater than the critical angle. Instead of refracting, the light is reflected back entirely within the denser medium.
 
• This principle is used in fiber optics and periscopes.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index of Common Materials:**
 
 
• The refractive index of air is approximately **1**, while that of glass typically ranges from **1.5 to 1.9**, depending on the type of glass.
 
• Diamond has one of the highest refractive indices, approximately **2.42**, which contributes to its brilliance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Refractive Phenomena in Nature:**

 
 
• **Rainbows:** Formed due to refraction, reflection, and dispersion of light in water droplets.
 
• **Twinkling of Stars:** Caused by the refraction of starlight through Earth’s turbulent atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Critical Angle:** The angle of incidence in the denser medium at which the angle of refraction becomes 90 degrees in the less dense medium.
 
• **Optical Density:** A measure of how much a material slows down light; higher optical density results in greater bending of light.

questions.question: A voltmeter is always connected in a circuit:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**in parallel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **voltmeter** is always connected in parallel__ with the component across which the potential difference is to be measured. This is because a voltmeter measures the voltage (potential difference) between two points in a circuit.
 
• The internal resistance of a voltmeter is designed to be very **high** to ensure that it draws negligible current from the circuit. This prevents any significant alteration in the circuit's current and voltage.
 
• If a voltmeter is connected __in series__, it would obstruct the flow of current due to its high resistance, which is not its intended use. *Hence, "in series" is incorrect.*
 
• Connecting a voltmeter "in place of a switch" or "in diagonal" is not a valid method of connection for measuring voltage. A switch is meant to control the flow of current, not measure potential difference. Similarly, diagonal connections are not relevant in standard electrical measurements. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• **In parallel** connection allows the voltmeter to measure the exact voltage drop across the component without significantly affecting the circuit's operation. *Hence, this is the correct option.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Voltmeter:**

 
 
• A voltmeter is an electrical instrument used to measure the **potential difference (voltage)** between two points in an electric circuit.
 
• It is commonly used in both **AC** and **DC circuits** to ensure components are operating at correct voltage levels.
 
 
 
• **Types of Voltmeters:**
 
 
• **Analog Voltmeter:** Uses a pointer and scale to display voltage readings.
 
• **Digital Voltmeter (DVM):** Provides numerical voltage readings on a digital display.
 
 
 
• **Importance of High Resistance:**
 
 
• The high internal resistance of a voltmeter ensures minimal current flows through it, preventing interference with the circuit's operation.
 
• For an ideal voltmeter, the resistance is considered **infinite**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Ammeter:**
 
 
• An ammeter, unlike a voltmeter, is connected **in series** and has very **low resistance** to measure the current without significant voltage drop.
 
• This fundamental difference in connection and resistance makes the voltmeter and ammeter complementary tools in circuit analysis.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Practical Applications:**

 
 
• Voltmeters are used in laboratories, industries, and home electrical systems to ensure proper voltage levels.
 
• In multimeters, voltmeters are integrated with other functions like current and resistance measurement, making them versatile tools.
 
 
 
• **Historical Development:**
 
 
• The invention of the voltmeter is attributed to the work of **Lord Kelvin** in the 19th century.
 
• Modern digital voltmeters were developed later in the 20th century with advancements in electronic circuits.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• Accuracy of analog voltmeters can be affected by parallax error.
 
• Digital voltmeters may face issues like noise and resolution limitations in high-frequency circuits.

questions.question: What is the role of the prostrate gland and seminal vesicles in the human male reproductive system?

options.text: To provide fluids for transporting sperm
To lower the temperature of the testes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide fluids for transporting sperm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **prostate gland** and **seminal vesicles** play a crucial role in the male reproductive system by producing fluids that aid in the transportation and nourishment of sperm.
 
• **Prostate gland:** It secretes a milky fluid that contributes to semen. This fluid enhances sperm motility and provides protection against the acidic environment of the female reproductive tract.
 
• **Seminal vesicles:** These glands produce a viscous, fructose-rich fluid that constitutes a significant portion of semen. Fructose serves as an energy source for sperm cells, allowing them to sustain their activity and reach the egg for fertilization.
 
• The combined fluids from the prostate gland and seminal vesicles help in sperm transportation by forming a medium in which sperm can swim efficiently during ejaculation.
 
• This function ensures successful reproduction by enhancing the survival and motility of sperm cells. *Hence, the correct statement is "To provide fluids for transporting sperm."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of Prostate Gland:**

 
 
• The prostate gland is located below the bladder and encircles the urethra. It secretes a fluid that is slightly alkaline, which helps neutralize the acidic pH of the female reproductive tract.
 
• The fluid contains **enzymes, zinc, and citric acid**, which support sperm function and longevity.
 
• Prostate-specific antigen (PSA), found in the prostate fluid, plays a role in liquefying semen after ejaculation to aid sperm motility.
 
 
 
• **Role of Seminal Vesicles:**
 
 
• The seminal vesicles are paired glands located behind the bladder. They secrete a fluid rich in **fructose, prostaglandins, and clotting proteins.**
 
• Fructose provides energy for sperm cells, while prostaglandins aid in stimulating muscle contractions in the female reproductive tract to facilitate sperm movement.
 
• Clotting proteins help semen coagulate immediately after ejaculation, ensuring sperm retention in the female tract before liquefaction occurs.
 
 
 
• **Other Functions:**
 
 
• Both the prostate gland and seminal vesicles work in synchronization to produce semen, which is expelled during ejaculation.
 
• These fluids not only provide nourishment and transportation but also protect sperm from environmental stressors.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **To secrete testosterone:** Testosterone is primarily produced by the **testes**, not the prostate gland or seminal vesicles.
 
• **To lower the temperature of the testes:** This function is performed by the **scrotum**, which regulates temperature for optimal sperm production.
 
• **To produce sperm cells:** Sperm cells are produced in the **seminiferous tubules** of the testes, not the prostate gland or seminal vesicles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prostate Gland Disorders:**

 
 
• Common issues include **prostatitis** (inflammation of the prostate) and **benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)**, a non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate.
 
• Prostate cancer is a significant health concern, particularly in men over the age of **50 years**.
 
 
 
• **Semen Composition:**
 
 
• Semen is composed of sperm cells (produced by the testes) and fluids from the prostate gland, seminal vesicles, and bulbourethral glands.
 
• A typical ejaculate contains **200 to 500 million sperm cells**, but only one is needed for fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Energy Requirement of Sperm:**
 
 
• The fructose produced by the seminal vesicles is critical for sperm motility. Without it, sperm would lack the energy to reach the egg.

questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of oxygen (Atomic number = 8)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1s² 2s² 2p⁴**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electronic Configuration:** Oxygen, with an **atomic number of 8**, has 8 electrons. The electronic configuration of oxygen is **1s² 2s² 2p⁴**.
 
• The electrons are distributed in shells according to the **Aufbau principle**, which fills orbitals in the order of increasing energy levels.
 
• The **1s orbital** is filled first with 2 electrons, followed by the **2s orbital** with 2 electrons, and finally, the remaining 4 electrons occupy the **2p orbital**.
 
• This configuration indicates that the **valence shell** of oxygen is the second shell (n=2), containing 6 electrons (2 in 2s and 4 in 2p).
 
• **Octet Rule:** Oxygen needs 2 more electrons to complete its octet, which explains its tendency to form compounds like H₂O (water) by sharing electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electronic Configuration Notation:**

 
 
• The notation **1s² 2s² 2p⁴** represents the distribution of electrons in various orbitals.
 
• Here, **1s²** means 2 electrons in the 1st shell's s-orbital, **2s²** means 2 electrons in the 2nd shell's s-orbital, and **2p⁴** means 4 electrons in the 2nd shell's p-orbital.
 
 
 
• **Valence Electrons:** Oxygen has **6 valence electrons** (2 from 2s and 4 from 2p), which participate in chemical bonding.
 
• **Periodic Table Placement:** Oxygen is in Group 16 (Chalcogens) and Period 2 of the periodic table. This placement reflects its properties and electronic configuration.
 
• **Oxidation State:** Oxygen commonly exhibits an oxidation state of **-2** in most compounds due to its high electronegativity.
 
• **Applications:** Oxygen is essential for respiration in living organisms and is widely used in industries such as medical oxygen supply, steel manufacturing, and water purification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aufbau Principle:** This principle dictates that electrons occupy orbitals in the order of increasing energy levels, starting from the lowest energy orbital.
 
• **Hund’s Rule:** In a subshell like 2p, electrons fill each orbital singly before pairing up to minimize repulsion and maximize stability.
 
• **Pauli Exclusion Principle:** No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers, ensuring unique arrangements in orbitals.
 
• **Bonding:** Oxygen forms both ionic and covalent bonds. For example, in H₂O, it shares electrons (covalent bonding), while in Na₂O, it accepts electrons (ionic bonding).

questions.question: If a man of mass 75 kg climbs an 8 m staircase in 25 s, taking g = 10 m/s² , his average power is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**120 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. It is calculated as **P = W / t**, where **W** is work done and **t** is time.
 
• The work done by the man in climbing the staircase is equal to the gravitational potential energy gained, given by **W = m × g × h**, where **m** is mass, **g** is acceleration due to gravity, and **h** is height.
 
• Substituting the values: **m = 75 kg, g = 10 m/s², h = 8 m**, we get **W = 75 × 10 × 8 = 6000 J**.
 
• Time taken to climb the staircase is given as **t = 25 seconds**.
 
• Average power is calculated as **P = W / t = 6000 / 25 = 240 W**.
 
• However, the correct answer in the options is **120 W**, indicating a potential discrepancy in either the question or the values provided. If the staircase height or time is adjusted, the calculated power might align with the options.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Power:**

 
 
• Measured in **Watts (W)**, where 1 Watt = 1 Joule/second.
 
• Power can be categorized into **average power** and **instantaneous power**. Average power is used in scenarios like climbing stairs, where energy is transferred over a duration.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy:**
 
 
• It is the energy possessed by an object due to its position in a gravitational field.
 
• Formula: **U = m × g × h**, where **m** is mass, **g** is acceleration due to gravity, and **h** is height.
 
 
 
• **Human Efficiency:**
 
 
• The actual power exerted by humans might differ due to efficiency losses, including friction and heat dissipation.
 
• For mechanical tasks like climbing stairs, efficiency usually ranges between **20%-30%**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Power Calculation:**
 
 
• Used in designing fitness programs to measure energy expenditure.
 
• Helps in calculating energy requirements for specific tasks, like building infrastructure or operating machinery.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unit of Power:** The SI unit is **Watt**, derived from the name of inventor James Watt.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** 1 Kilowatt-hour (kWh) is equal to **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**, a unit often used in electricity billing.
 
• **Practical Examples:**
 
 
• A 100-Watt bulb consumes **100 Joules** of energy per second.
 
• Humans typically generate around **100-300 W** of power during moderate physical activity.

questions.question: What type of reaction is CaO + H₂O rightarrow Ca(OH)₂ ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction **CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂** is a **Combination Reaction**, where two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO)**, commonly known as quicklime, reacts with water (H₂O) to form **calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂)**, also called slaked lime.
 
• In a combination reaction, the individual reactants (in this case, CaO and H₂O) lose their identities to form a new compound (Ca(OH)₂).
 
• Combination reactions are typically exothermic, meaning they release heat. In this reaction, heat is released, making the solution warm or even hot.
 
• **General formula of a combination reaction:** A + B → AB. Here, CaO (A) combines with H₂O (B) to form Ca(OH)₂ (AB).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Combination Reaction:**

 
 
• A type of chemical reaction where **two or more substances combine** to form a single product.
 
• Examples include:
 
 
• Formation of water: H₂ + O₂ → H₂O
 
• Formation of carbon dioxide: C + O₂ → CO₂
 
 
 
• Such reactions play a significant role in processes like corrosion, biological synthesis, and industrial manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂):**
 
 
• Commonly known as slaked lime, it is used in **construction, wastewater treatment,** and as a neutralizing agent in industries.
 
• It is slightly soluble in water, forming a suspension known as limewater.
 
• Limewater is used to test for the presence of carbon dioxide, as it turns milky when CO₂ is bubbled through it.
 
 
 
• **Other Reaction Types:**
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction:** A reaction where one element replaces another in a compound. Example: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:** A reaction where an acid reacts with a base to form salt and water. Example: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.
 
• **Decomposition Reaction:** A reaction where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. Example: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Combination Reactions:**
 
 
• Used in the **manufacture of cement** and other construction materials.
 
• Important in **metallurgy**, where metals combine with other substances to form useful alloys.
 
• Used in **agriculture** to prepare fertilizers like calcium phosphate.

questions.question: Why do we need to conserve coal and petroleum?

options.text: They are renewable sources of energy.

They are non-renewable sources of energy.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are non-renewable sources of energy.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coal and petroleum are classified as non-renewable resources** because they take millions of years to form through geological processes and cannot be replenished on a human timescale.
 
• These resources are derived from the remains of ancient plants and animals that were buried under layers of earth and subjected to high pressure and temperature over millions of years. 
 
• **Excessive usage** of coal and petroleum without conservation leads to depletion, making them unavailable for future generations. 
 
• Coal and petroleum are extensively used for generating energy, powering industries, transportation, and domestic purposes, which increases their demand and accelerates their consumption. 
 
• **Environmental impact:** Burning coal and petroleum releases greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane, contributing to climate change and air pollution. 
 
• Conserving these resources encourages the development of alternative energy sources such as solar, wind, and hydropower, reducing dependence on fossil fuels. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of coal:** Coal is formed from plant remains buried in swampy areas millions of years ago. Through processes of compaction and heat, these remains transform into peat and eventually into coal.
 
• **Formation of petroleum:** Petroleum originates from the remains of marine organisms buried under sediments. Over millions of years, heat and pressure convert these remains into hydrocarbons, forming crude oil and natural gas. 
 
• **Types of coal:** Coal is categorized into four types based on carbon content and heating value: lignite, sub-bituminous, bituminous, and anthracite. Anthracite has the highest carbon content and is considered the most efficient for energy production. 
 
• **Uses of coal and petroleum:**
 
 
• Coal is used for electricity generation, steel manufacturing, cement production, and as fuel for industrial processes. 
 
• Petroleum is refined into products like gasoline, diesel, kerosene, and jet fuel, and is used in industries such as transportation, plastics, and pharmaceuticals. 
 
 
 
• **Global reserves:**
 
 
• Coal reserves are concentrated in countries like the **United States, Russia, China, and India**. India ranks fifth globally in coal reserves.
 
• Major petroleum-producing countries include **Saudi Arabia, Russia, the United States, Iran, and Canada**. The Middle East is known for its vast petroleum reserves.
 
 
 
• **Environmental concerns:**
 
 
• Mining coal leads to habitat destruction, soil erosion, and water pollution. 
 
• Oil spills during petroleum extraction and transportation cause severe harm to aquatic ecosystems. 
 
• Burning fossil fuels contributes significantly to global warming and acid rain. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Government initiatives:**
 
 
• The **National Solar Mission** promotes the use of solar energy to reduce dependence on coal and petroleum. 
 
• The **Perform, Achieve, and Trade (PAT) Scheme** under the National Mission on Enhanced Energy Efficiency aims to improve energy efficiency in industries, indirectly conserving coal and petroleum. 
 
 
 
• **International perspective:** The **Paris Agreement** emphasizes reducing carbon emissions by minimizing the use of fossil fuels and transitioning to renewable energy sources. Countries worldwide are adopting policies to conserve non-renewable resources. 
 
• **Alternatives to fossil fuels:**
 
 
• Renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and hydropower are sustainable and environmentally friendly. 
 
• Biofuels derived from organic matter are being explored as substitutes for petroleum-based fuels.

questions.question: Which of the following methods is NOT used for the ore enrichment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dredging**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dredging** is not a method used for ore enrichment. It is a process primarily used in clearing sediments and debris from the bottom of lakes, rivers, and other water bodies, often to maintain navigable waterways or to reclaim land.
 
• **Hydraulic washing**, also known as gravity separation, is a method of ore enrichment that separates lighter impurities from heavier ore particles by washing them with water. *Hence, it is used for ore enrichment.*
 
• **Froth flotation** is a widely used process for enriching ores, particularly sulfide ores. It involves mixing crushed ores with water and chemicals to create a froth where the ore particles attach to bubbles and float, separating them from impurities. *This is a correct method for ore enrichment.*
 
• **Leaching** is a chemical process used in ore enrichment where the desired metal is dissolved in a solvent, leaving behind impurities. For example, the cyanide process is used to extract gold and silver. *This is also a valid method for ore enrichment.*
 
• **Dredging** does not play any role in ore enrichment and is used in environmental or civil engineering applications rather than in metallurgy or mining. **Hence, it is the correct answer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydraulic Washing:**

 
 
• This method is based on the difference in densities between the ore and the gangue particles.
 
• It is effective for ores like hematite and tin stone, which are heavier than the impurities.
 
• It uses water flow to wash away lighter impurities, leaving behind the heavier ore particles.

• Primarily used for sulfide ores like copper, zinc, and lead.
 
• Involves the addition of collectors like pine oil and frothers to enhance the formation of froth.
 
• The ore particles attach to air bubbles and are carried to the surface, while impurities sink to the bottom.
 
 
 
• **Leaching:**
 
 
• Commonly used in the extraction of metals like gold, silver, and aluminum.
 
• For example, in the Bayer process, bauxite is leached with sodium hydroxide to extract aluminum oxide.
 
• Leaching is highly selective and effective for low-grade ores.
 
 
 
• **Dredging:**
 
 
• A mechanical process used to remove sediments or debris from water bodies.
 
• It is used for deepening waterways, preventing flooding, or reclaiming land for construction projects.
 
• While it involves excavation, it is unrelated to the enrichment of ores in metallurgical processes.

questions.question: Small changes in DNA copies during reproduction are important because they ________.

options.text: stop reproduction in the next generation
provide variations which may help in survival

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**provide variations which may help in survival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Small changes in DNA during reproduction, also called **genetic variations**, are critical for the survival of species. These variations introduce differences in the offspring compared to their parents.
 
• Genetic variations can create traits that are advantageous in certain environmental conditions, increasing the **survival and adaptability** of the species.
 
• Over time, these beneficial variations can accumulate and lead to **evolution**, allowing species to adapt to changing environments and ecological niches.
 
• This process is central to the theory of **natural selection**, as proposed by Charles Darwin, where organisms with advantageous traits are more likely to survive and reproduce.
 
• Without these small changes in DNA, populations could become genetically identical, limiting their ability to cope with changing environments, diseases, or predators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA and Genetic Variation:**

 
 
• **DNA** (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the molecule that carries the genetic instructions for growth, reproduction, and functioning of all living organisms.
 
• Genetic variations occur due to **mutations**, genetic recombination during sexual reproduction, and other factors like environmental influences.
 
• Mutations can be **neutral**, beneficial, or harmful, but beneficial mutations contribute to the adaptation of species over time.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Genetic Variation:**
 
 
• In humans, variations in skin color, eye color, and blood types are examples of genetic diversity.
 
• In agriculture, genetic variation in crops like wheat and rice has been utilized to develop varieties resistant to pests and environmental stresses.
 
 
 
• **Role of Natural Selection:**
 
 
• Natural selection is the process by which organisms with traits better suited to their environment tend to survive and reproduce more than others.
 
• Over generations, this leads to an increase in the frequency of advantageous traits, driving the **evolution of species**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Genetic Variation in Evolution:**
 
 
• Genetic variation provides the raw material for evolution. Without it, species cannot adapt to changes in their environment.
 
• For instance, antibiotic resistance in bacteria is a result of genetic variation that allows some bacteria to survive and reproduce in the presence of antibiotics.
 
 
 
• **Other Factors Influencing Genetic Variation:**
 
 
• Genetic drift, gene flow, and mutation rates also play critical roles in shaping the genetic makeup of populations.
 
• Environmental factors such as climate, availability of resources, and interactions with other species can also influence which genetic variations are advantageous.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by binary fission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary fission** is a mode of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into two equal and identical daughter cells.
 
• **Amoeba**, a unicellular organism, reproduces by binary fission. During this process, its nucleus divides by mitosis, followed by the division of the cytoplasm, resulting in two identical cells.
 
• Binary fission in Amoeba occurs under favorable conditions such as adequate temperature, moisture, and nutrient availability.
 
• Unlike Amoeba, organisms like **Spirogyra** reproduce through fragmentation, **Hydra** via budding, and **Planaria** through regeneration. Hence, these organisms do not reproduce by binary fission.
 
• Binary fission ensures the rapid multiplication of organisms, allowing them to adapt quickly to favorable environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amoeba:**

 
 
• Amoeba is a **unicellular protozoan** that belongs to the kingdom Protista.
 
• It is found in freshwater, soil, and marine environments.
 
• The organism has an irregular shape and moves using temporary projections of its cytoplasm called **pseudopodia**.
 
• Amoeba can survive harsh conditions by forming a **protective cyst**, a process known as encystation.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission:**
 
 
• Binary fission is a simple and efficient mode of asexual reproduction commonly observed in prokaryotes like bacteria and some eukaryotes like Amoeba and Paramecium.
 
• It involves three main steps: replication of the genetic material, elongation of the cell, and division into two daughter cells.
 
• There are different types of binary fission based on the plane of division: **simple binary fission** (irregular plane, seen in Amoeba), **transverse binary fission** (horizontal plane, seen in Paramecium), and **longitudinal binary fission** (vertical plane, seen in Euglena).
 
 
 
• **Spirogyra:**
 
 
• Spirogyra is a **filamentous green alga** that reproduces mainly through fragmentation and sexual reproduction (conjugation).
 
• In fragmentation, each broken filament develops into a new organism.
 
 
 
• **Hydra:**
 
 
• Hydra reproduces asexually through **budding**, where a small outgrowth (bud) develops on the parent body and eventually detaches to become an independent organism.
 
 
 
• **Planaria:**
 
 
• Planaria exhibits **regeneration**, where it can regrow lost body parts or develop into a complete organism from a small fragment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Binary fission vs Other Modes of Asexual Reproduction:**

 
 
• **Binary fission:** A parent cell splits into two equal halves (e.g., Amoeba).
 
• **Budding:** A small bud forms on the parent organism and detaches (e.g., Hydra).
 
• **Fragmentation:** The organism breaks into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new organism (e.g., Spirogyra).
 
• **Regeneration:** The ability of an organism to regrow lost parts or form a new organism from fragments (e.g., Planaria).

questions.question: The formula for acceleration due to gravity (g) at the surface of the Earth is ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**g = GM/R²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g)** is the force exerted by the Earth on objects at its surface, causing them to fall toward the ground.
 
• The formula **g = GM/R²** expresses the relationship between gravitational constant (**G**), Earth's mass (**M**), and Earth's radius (**R**).
 
• **Gravitational constant (G):** A universal constant with a value of approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg².
 
• **Earth's mass (M):** Approximately 5.972 × 10²⁴ kg, which contributes to the gravitational pull experienced by objects.
 
• **Earth's radius (R):** The average radius of Earth is approximately 6,371 km or 6.371 × 10⁶ m.
 
• The formula demonstrates that **g is inversely proportional to the square of the radius**, meaning that gravitational acceleration decreases as the distance from Earth's center increases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Variation of g with altitude:**

 
 
• The value of g decreases as altitude increases because the distance from Earth's center increases.
 
• For small changes in altitude, g at height h can be approximated by **g' = g(1 - 2h/R)**.
 
 
 
• **Variation of g with latitude:**
 
 
• Earth is not a perfect sphere but an oblate spheroid, meaning g is slightly higher at the poles and lower at the equator.
 
• This variation is due to Earth's rotation and its equatorial bulge.
 
 
 
• **Effect of Earth's rotation:**
 
 
• Earth’s rotation causes a centrifugal force that slightly reduces g at the equator.
 
• The effective value of g decreases with an increase in rotational speed.
 
 
 
• **Practical applications of g:**
 
 
• Used in calculating free-fall motion, projectile motion, and orbital mechanics.
 
• Essential for designing rockets and satellites by considering gravitational forces.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gravitational constant (G):** First measured by **Henry Cavendish** in 1798 using the torsion balance experiment.
 
• **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation:** States that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• **Galileo’s observations:** Showed that all objects fall at the same rate in the absence of air resistance, proving the uniformity of gravitational acceleration.
 
• **Applications in space missions:** The value of g and gravitational forces are critical in planning interplanetary missions and calculating escape velocity (approximately 11.2 km/s for Earth).

__
 
• **A molecule of water (H₂O)** consists of **3 atoms**: two hydrogen (H) atoms and one oxygen (O) atom.
 
• **Chemical composition:** Water’s molecular formula, H₂O, clearly indicates that it is made up of **2 hydrogen atoms** and **1 oxygen atom**.
 
• **Covalent bonding:** The hydrogen and oxygen atoms in water are held together by **covalent bonds**, where electrons are shared between the atoms.
 
• **Structural arrangement:** The water molecule has a **bent or V-shaped structure** due to the electron pair repulsion around the oxygen atom, which results in a bond angle of approximately **104.5°**.
 
• **Importance of the composition:** The exact atomic composition and structure of water contribute to its unique properties, such as its polarity, high boiling point, and ability to act as a universal solvent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen atoms in water:**

 
 
• Each hydrogen atom in a water molecule contributes **one electron** to form a covalent bond with the oxygen atom.
 
• Hydrogen is the lightest element and plays a crucial role in forming water’s molecular structure.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen atom in water:**
 
 
• The oxygen atom is more **electronegative** than hydrogen, meaning it pulls the shared electrons closer to itself.
 
• This causes a partial negative charge on oxygen and a partial positive charge on hydrogen, making water a **polar molecule**.
 
 
 
• **Polarity of water:**
 
 
• Due to its bent shape and difference in electronegativity, water is a **polar molecule**.
 
• This polarity allows water to dissolve many substances, making it a **universal solvent**.
 
 
 
• **Unique properties due to structure:**
 
 
• The hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules result in properties like **high surface tension**, **capillary action**, and **high boiling and freezing points**.
 
• These properties are essential for life on Earth and many biological processes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of water’s molecular structure:**
 
 
• Water’s polarity makes it essential for **cellular processes** such as nutrient transport and biochemical reactions.
 
• Its unique structure supports the formation of hydrogen bonds, vital for the structure of **DNA and proteins**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Water as a compound:** Water is a **compound**, not an element, because it consists of more than one type of atom chemically bonded together.
 
• **Molecular weight:** The molecular weight of water is approximately **18 g/mol** (2 hydrogen atoms weighing ~1 g/mol each + 1 oxygen atom weighing ~16 g/mol).
 
• **Water’s role in life:** It is indispensable for life, being a major component of cells, and is involved in essential processes like **photosynthesis** and **cellular respiration**.
 
• **Physical states:** Water exists in all three states of matter—solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapor)—at **Earth’s natural temperature range**.

questions.question: The absolute refractive index of a medium is defined as the ratio of ___________.

options.text: speed of light in vacuum to speed of light in medium
speed of light in water to speed of light in medium
speed of light in glass to speed of light in water
speed of light in medium to speed of light in vacuum

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**speed of light in vacuum to speed of light in medium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **absolute refractive index** of a medium is defined as the ratio of the **speed of light in a vacuum** to the **speed of light in the medium**.
 
• **Mathematically:** Refractive index (n) = c/v, where **c** is the speed of light in vacuum (approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s) and **v** is the speed of light in the given medium.
 
• This property is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced in a particular medium compared to a vacuum.
 
• The refractive index is dimensionless and always greater than or equal to 1, as light travels fastest in a vacuum.
 
• The refractive index affects phenomena like **refraction**, where light bends when transitioning between mediums of different refractive indices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed of Light in Different Media:**

 
 
• In **vacuum**, the speed of light is approximately **3 × 10⁸ m/s**.
 
• In **air**, the speed of light is slightly less than in a vacuum but is often approximated as the same for practical purposes.
 
• In **water**, the speed of light is approximately **2.25 × 10⁸ m/s**, giving water a refractive index of about 1.33.
 
• In **glass**, the speed of light is around **2 × 10⁸ m/s**, with a refractive index of approximately 1.5.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Vacuum:** A space devoid of matter where light travels at its maximum speed.
 
• **Medium:** A material (e.g., air, water, glass) through which light propagates.
 
• **Refractive Index:** A measure of how much light slows down and bends when entering a medium from a vacuum or another medium.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Refractive Index:**
 
 
• Used in designing optical devices such as **lenses** and **prisms**.
 
• Important in **fiber optic technology** for data transmission.
 
• Helps in studying the **composition of materials** and their optical properties.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• The refractive index of diamond is around **2.42**, making it highly effective in bending light and contributing to its brilliance.
 
• Refractive index is also used in **measuring the purity of substances**, such as liquids in industries.

The correct answer is __**Lysosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound cell organelles that contain **digestive enzymes**. These enzymes break down excess or worn-out cell parts, as well as foreign invaders like bacteria or viruses.
 
• They act as the **clean-up system of the cell** by digesting and removing cellular debris and foreign materials, ensuring the cell remains healthy and free from harmful substances.
 
• The enzymes in lysosomes are capable of digesting **proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids**, which makes them essential for cellular metabolism and recycling.
 
• Lysosomes are often referred to as the **"suicidal bags of the cell"** because they can self-destruct by releasing their enzymes if the cell is damaged or in a state of emergency.
 
• Their role in **autophagy (self-eating)** is crucial for the recycling of old or damaged organelles, maintaining cellular health and energy balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chloroplast:**

 
 
• Chloroplasts are **green, double-membrane organelles** found in plant cells and some algae.
 
• They are responsible for **photosynthesis**, a process that converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

• They are not involved in the digestion or recycling of cellular materials.
 
 
 
• **Ribosome:**
 
 
• Ribosomes are the **protein synthesis machinery** of the cell, either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• They are composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins**.
 
• They are not involved in cellular digestion or cleaning functions.
 
 
 
• **Chromoplast:**
 
 
• Chromoplasts are specialized organelles in plants that contain pigments other than chlorophyll, such as **carotenoids**, which give fruits and flowers their bright colors.
 
• They play a role in **attracting pollinators** but do not have any role in cellular digestion or cleaning.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Lysosomes:**
 
 
• Lysosomes help in **defense mechanisms** by digesting harmful bacteria and viruses.
 
• They are involved in **programmed cell death (apoptosis)**, which is essential for the removal of damaged cells in multicellular organisms.
 
• They contribute to **metabolic processes** by breaking down macromolecules into their monomers for reuse by the cell.

questions.question: The average age of a father and his daughter is 27 years. The ratio of their ages 4 years hence from now, will be 23 : 8. Find the daughter's present age (in years).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present sum of ages = 27 × 2 = 54 years.

Sum of ages after 4 years = 54 + 8 = 62 years.

Total ratio parts after 4 years = 23 + 8 = 31 parts.

31 parts = 62 years ⇒ 1 part = 2 years.

Daughter's present age = (8 parts × 2) − 4 = 12 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average present age of father and daughter = 27 years

Ratio of their ages 4 years hence = 23 : 8

 Ages 4 Years Hence Total Sum = 54 (Present) + 8 = 62 years Father (23 units) 8 units 
 Total 31 units = 62 years → 1 unit = 2 years Daughter's Present Age = (8 × 2) − 4 = 12 years 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of their present ages = 27 × 2 = 54 years

⇒ Let the present age of the father be F and the daughter be D.

⇒ F + D = 54

⇒ After 4 years, Father's age = F + 4 and Daughter's age = D + 4

⇒ (F + 4) / (D + 4) = 23 / 8

⇒ 8 × (F + 4) = 23 × (D + 4)

⇒ 8F + 32 = 23D + 92

⇒ 8F − 23D = 60

⇒ Substituting F = 54 − D into the equation:

⇒ 8 × (54 − D) − 23D = 60

⇒ 432 − 8D − 23D = 60

⇒ 31D = 432 − 60

⇒ 31D = 372

⇒ D = 372 ÷ 31 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Ages Over Time

If the sum of ages of n people is S, then their sum of ages after t years will be S + nt, because each person's age increases by t years independently.

Change in Average Age

If the present average age of a group is A, their average age after t years will exactly be A + t. The new total sum will naturally be n × (A + t).

Age Ratio Interpretation

When setting up linear equations from word problems, "t years hence" always requires adding t to the present age variables, while "t years ago" requires subtracting t from the present age variables before applying any ratio comparison.

**Formula Used:**

Let the two consecutive integers be x and (x + 1).

⇒ x + (x + 1) = 51

⇒ 2x + 1 = 51

⇒ 2x = 51 − 1

⇒ 2x = 50

⇒ x = 50 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 25

The first number is 25.

⇒ The second number = x + 1 = 25 + 1 = 26.

**∴ The correct answer is 25, 26.**

Consecutive Integers

Numbers that follow each other continuously in order from smallest to largest without any gaps. They can be represented algebraically as x, x + 1, x + 2, etc.

Consecutive Even or Odd Integers

The difference between consecutive even or consecutive odd integers is always 2. They can be represented algebraically as x, x + 2, x + 4, etc.

Average of Uniform Sequences

The average of any uniformly spaced sequence (such as consecutive integers) is exactly equal to its middle value, or the sum of the first and last terms divided by 2.

questions.question: If x² + (1)/(x²) = 47 , then a possible value of (x + (1)/(x)) is:

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2

Substitute the given value x² + 1/x² = 47:

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 47 + 2

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 49

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ x + 1/x = ±7

questions.question: Which of the following tennis tournaments used live electronic line calling instead of human judges in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wimbledon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All England Lawn Tennis Club (AELTC)** announced in **October 2024** that it would replace human line judges with **Live Electronic Line Calling (Live ELC)** starting from the **2025** Championships.
 
• This historic decision ends **147 years** of tradition at **Wimbledon**, where line judges in their iconic uniforms have been a staple of the grass-court tournament since its inception in **1877**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Wimbledon is correct.***
 
• The new **Live ELC** system will be utilized on all **18 show courts** as well as the **qualifying** rounds held at **Roehampton**.
 
• The move is designed to ensure maximum accuracy in officiating, providing a consistent environment for players who have become accustomed to the technology on the **ATP** and **WTA** tours.
 
• Approximately **300 line judges** who worked the tournament annually will no longer be required, though **Chair Umpires** will remain in place to manage the match and keep the official score.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Australian Open and US Open:**
 
 
• The **Australian Open** became the first **Grand Slam** to entirely replace line judges with **Live ELC** in **2021**, partly as a response to the **COVID-19 pandemic** to reduce on-court personnel.
 
• The **US Open** followed suit in **2021**, adopting the technology across all its courts in **New York** to streamline play and reduce officiating errors.
 
 
 
• **The French Open (Roland Garros):**
 
 
• As of **2025**, the **French Open** remains the only **Grand Slam** to continue using human line judges.
 
• Because it is played on **clay**, the tournament relies on the physical mark the ball leaves on the surface, which the **Chair Umpire** can manually inspect if a call is disputed.
 
 
 
• **ATP Tour Mandate:**
 
 
• The **ATP Tour** (men’s professional circuit) previously announced a universal mandate that all **ATP** events must adopt **Electronic Line Calling** by the year **2025**.
 
• This policy aims to provide uniformity across various surfaces and tournament tiers, from **ATP 250** to **Masters 1000** events.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hawk-Eye Technology:** Most **Live ELC** systems are powered by **Hawk-Eye Innovations**, which uses multiple high-speed cameras to track the trajectory of the ball and trigger an automated "out" voice call within **one-tenth of a second**.
 
• **Removal of Challenges:** With the implementation of **Live ELC**, the traditional "challenge" system (where players ask for a video review) is eliminated, as every call is essentially a real-time review.
 
• **Game Speed:** Data indicates that **Live ELC** significantly speeds up the duration of matches by reducing the time spent on disputes and the physical movement of line judges during changeovers.
 
• **Preservation of Tradition:** While **Wimbledon** is moving to digital officiating, the **AELTC** emphasized that the **Chair Umpire** remains the final authority on court for matters of conduct and scorekeeping.

questions.question: What responsibility did the Supreme Court give to the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) in April 2025?

options.text: To study the impact of glass industries on the Taj Mahal
To relocate glass factories near the Taj Mahal
To promote tourism near the Taj Mahal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To study the impact of glass industries on the Taj Mahal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** issued a directive to the **National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI)** to conduct a detailed scientific assessment.
 
• The primary responsibility assigned to **NEERI** was to **study the impact of glass industries** on the structural integrity and aesthetic preservation of the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• This study focuses on the environmental footprint of industrial units located within the **Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ)**, specifically those involved in glass manufacturing in nearby regions like **Firozabad**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the impact of glass industries is correct.***
 
• The **Supreme Court** aims to determine if the emissions from these industries are contributing to the yellowing of the marble or "**marble cancer**," caused by chemical reactions with pollutants.
 
• **NEERI** is expected to provide data-driven recommendations on whether existing pollution control equipment in these factories is sufficient or if stricter regulations are required to protect the **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI):**
 
 
• It was established in **1958** and is headquartered in **Nagpur**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• It functions under the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)** and focuses on environmental monitoring, hazardous waste management, and environmental impact assessments.
 
• **NEERI** has been frequently consulted by the **Indian Judiciary** for expert technical opinions on environmental conservation cases.
 
 
 
• **The Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ):**
 
 
• The **TTZ** is a defined area of approximately **10,400 square kilometers** around the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• It encompasses several districts including **Agra**, **Firozabad**, **Mathura**, **Hathras**, and **Etah** in **Uttar Pradesh**, as well as **Bharatpur** in **Rajasthan**.
 
• The zone was established following the **1996 Supreme Court** judgment to protect the monument from pollution-induced damage.
 
 
 
• **Glass Industry in Firozabad:**
 
 
• **Firozabad** is known as the "**Glass City of India**" due to its extensive cluster of glass-making units and bangle factories.
 
• Historically, these industries used **coal** and **coke**, which emitted high levels of **Sulfur Dioxide (SO2)** and **particulate matter**, posing a direct threat to the white marble of the **Taj Mahal**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Precedents:** The protection of the **Taj Mahal** is governed by the landmark case of **M.C. Mehta vs. Union of India**, filed in the **1980s**, which led to the closure of several polluting industries.
 
• **Transition to Cleaner Fuel:** The **Supreme Court** previously mandated that industries in the **TTZ** must switch from traditional fuels to **Piped Natural Gas (PNG)** to minimize the carbon footprint and acidic emissions.
 
• **Marble Cancer:** This term refers to the corrosion of marble by **acid rain** (formed by **Sulfur Dioxide** and **Nitrogen Oxides** reacting with water vapor), which converts calcium carbonate into calcium sulfate, causing the surface to flake and turn yellow.
 
• **Current Status:** The **April 2025** order signifies the court's ongoing vigilance in balancing industrial economic activity with the preservation of **India's** cultural heritage through rigorous scientific auditing by **CSIR-NEERI**.
</ul

• **Medical Aid**: A significant part of the relief package included **Level-2 and Level-3 medical facilities** capable of performing emergency surgeries in field conditions.
